full_judgment:
Respondent No.3, IFIC Bank Limited, being Financial Institution, filed a Artha Rin Suit No. 25 of 1997 against the petitioner and others for recovery of loan amount to the tune of Taka 45,86,60,687 as on 21-12-1996 by selling the mortgage property of the petitioner and others and ultimately the suit was decreed ex-parte on 22-2-2009 with a further direction to pay the decretal amount within 60 days. On the failure to pay the decretal amount amicably the decree holder filed execution Case No. 14 of2009 on 26-8-2009 for the purpose of recovery of the decretal amount with interest up to 20-8-2009 to the tune of Taka ,1,16,40,72,416 where judgment debtor-petitioners made their appearance and filed an objection therein but rejecting it on 24-6-2012 a decision was taken to put the mortgage property in auction under 33(1) of the' Artha Rin Adalat Ain,2003 for which notice was published in daily news paper fixing the date on 2-8-2012. 

 3. Subsequently on 5-7-2012 the judgment debtor petitioner again filed an application under Order XXI, rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 with a prayer to issue a certificate under Order XXI, rule 83(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure to sell the mortgage property by "Private Negotiation" to raise amount of decree but on 8-7-2012 such prayer is found to have been disposed of; as being not pressed. Thereafter, the petitioner judgment debtor again filed an application for stay the auction sale with a commitment to dispose of this execution case by mediation. 

 5. Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that if certificate is issued under Order XXI, rule 83(2) it will be most convenient on the part of the judgment debtor to sell the "registered mortgage-properly" as well as the equitable mortgage-property at a higher rate than that of the court sale though it may not cover the entire amount of Taka 1,16,40,72,416.00 for which the execution case has been filed. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner further submits that since there is no specific direction in the decree to sell the property in auction the provision of Order XXI, rule 83 read with section 26 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 will certainly come to play facilitating the judgment-debtor to raise the decretal amount in question. Moreover, there is a negotiation with the decree holder to settle the matter outside the court; as such it is required to stop the auction sale through court under section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 6. On the other hand, Mr Md Kabir Iqbal Hossain the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Respondent No.3 has strongly opposed the Rule alleging inter alia that in order to drag the Execution case involving huge amount of Taka 1l6,40,72.416 as on 20-8-2009 the judgment debtor has been adopting this dilatory tactics which should not be allowed to continue. Mr Kabir has drawn the attention of the court that this suit for recovery of money by sale of mortgage properly was filed in the early part of 1997 for recovery of outstanding loan to the tune of Taka 45,86,60,687 as on 31-12-1996 and now on the date of execution it has become to Taka 1,16,40,72,416 as on 20-8-2009 but yet the decree holder has failed to get the execution case disposed of on full satisfaction rather the petitioner has come to file this type of application under Order XXI, rule 83 more than one occasion with an intention to drag the execution case. Moreover, Order XXI, rule 83(3) has totally excluded the instant matter out of the clutch of rule 83(2) of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure and also will be in conflict with the provisions of section 37 of the Ain, 2003 where time limit has been prescribed for disposal of execution case. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has also referred an unreported decision of a case Razi Abul Hossain vs Standard Chartered Bank in Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 1868 of 2002 where their lordships of the Apex Court have made the following observation:- 

 "Where the decree contains a specific provision as to the sale of the property, the Court has no discretion in the matter and that upon reading the provision of Order XXI,rule 83 and the decision cited above the inescapable conclusion is that under sub-Rule 3 the provision of Order 83 is not applicable in the instant case." 

 "The expressions the amount of the decree may be raised' used in sub-rule (1) means the total decretal amount and not an amount which could not satisfy the decree, and no Court can grant such permission unless the entire debt can be realized by private alienation. This provision should be read subject to the provision of sub-rule (3) which is a non-obstante clause, which provides "Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of, or charge on, such property". 

 So, sub-rule (1) does not apply to cases in which properly is directed to be sold in execution of a decree on a mortgage. This is because, the decree-holder or the creditor's right of sale rests on the decree. If the judgment-debtor effected the alienation with the consent of the decree-holder, the implication of such sale would be otherwise. This is because by giving consent to the private sale the decree-holder docs not become a holder of the decree for payment of money which is an essential condition for the applicability of section 73 of the Code. Therefore, there is no doubt that in case of a decree for foreclosure, be if the High Court Division, or any other superior Court, it has no power to issue certificate to alienate the mortgaged property for enabling the judgment-debtor to raise money for payment of the total decretal amount by private sale without the consent of the decree-holder. The High Court Division had totally overlooked this bar and erroneously directed for the issuance of sale certificate in favour of the judgment-debtor. The direction . was also exercised without affording the decree-holder bank an opportunity to defend the order and therefore, this order had no sanctity of law and the decree holder was not bound by the said direction. Similarly, no right, title and interest in respect of the mortgaged property was conferred upon the purchaser Ragib Ali on the strength of the deed which was allegedly executed by the judgment debtor on the strength of an illegal sale certificate; it was issued in total violation of law." 

 8. Having due regard to the above decision of our Apex Court we are also to say that sub-rule (3) of rule 83 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly has excluded the application of the Order XXI, rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure in a case where decree itself provides specific provision to sell the mortgage property for recovery of decretal amount. In the instant case the claim of the plaintiff as shown in the plaint is for recovery of money by sale of the mortgage property and accordingly the impugned decree was passed in the following language:- 

 9. In fact, the operating portion of the judgment and decree clearly indicates how the decretal amount can be realised and accordingly the decree-holder filed an Execution Case No. 14 of 2009 on 27-8-2009 following all the mandatory provisions laid down in Ain, 2003 and ultimately by issuing a notice upon all the judgment-debtors put the mortgage property in auction under section 33(1) of the Ain, 2003. In such situation importing the provision laid down in Order XXI, rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure none can be allowed to circumvent the statutory provision laid down in special Ain, 2003. Even the decision of the Apex court has clearly and unambiguously opined that where the decree has been passed containing the specific provision to sell the property in enforcement of mortgage of or charge on, such property, there can be no scope to bring the matter within the mischief of Order XXI, rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. 

 (3) উপ-ধারা (২) এর অধীন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক দায়েরকৃত মামলা নিষ্ক্রিয় সমাপ্তির (Foreclosure) উদ্দেশ্যে একটি বন্ধকী মামলা (Mortgage Suit) হইলে, কেবলমাত্র সেইক্ষেত্রে আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রী প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী (preliminary decree) হইবে এবং অন্যান্য সকল ক্ষেত্রে ঋণ আদায়ার্থ দায়েরকৃত মামলায় আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রী (Final decree) হইবে। 

 12. The above provisions of law has clearly brought the matter within the scope of sub-rule (3) of rule 83 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 since the property in question is directed to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on such property. It reveals from sub-rule (3) of rule 83 that other provision laid down in sub-rule (1) & (2) of the rule 83 of order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 does not, at all, apply to a sale in enforcement of a mortgage decree. Sub- rule (3) of rule 83 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 is quoted below:- 

 "(3) Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to' apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in executing of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or Change on, such property." 

 13. Now let us also quote the provision laid down in section 26 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 regarding the applicability of the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for the purpose of the execution of a decree filed in the Artha Rin Adalat.
